subject.title: Cross-provider fallback should respect provider trust boundaries for images/attachments

question: Should cross-provider model fallback preserve current media forwarding unless users opt into a new provider media trust policy, or should OpenClaw strip/suppress media by default whenever fallback crosses providers?
rationale: Both choices affect the security boundary and existing fallback compatibility, and repository policy treats fallback behavior and new config/default surfaces as maintainer-sensitive.

options.title: Add explicit media trust policy
options.body: Preserve compatibility by default unless maintainers choose a migration, and add tested config/docs so operators can restrict images and attachments crossing provider boundaries.

options.title: Fail closed on cross-provider media
options.body: Strip explicit and prompt-detected media by default on cross-provider fallback, accepting a compatibility change with upgrade proof and clear docs.

options.title: Reject a core policy knob
options.body: Document that users needing media isolation should avoid cross-provider fallbacks or run separate agents/gateways, leaving the runtime behavior unchanged.

recommendation.title: Add explicit media trust policy
recommendation.body: Preserve compatibility by default unless maintainers choose a migration, and add tested config/docs so operators can restrict images and attachments crossing provider boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent owns the most recent current-main changes on the affected fallback media path and can route the security/product choice to secops if needed.
